tx_little_guide_s_wall.blurb: Little Guide's Wall is one of the more distant walls on the North Shore side of Reimers Ranch, west of Austin. It holds 19 climbs, nearly all bolted single-pitch sport lines, plus one top rope and a single boulder problem. Grades cover a broad range: a couple of easy routes in the 5.6 to 5.7 range, a handful of 5.9s, and a solid block of 5.10s and 5.11s that makes up most of the wall. Several small roofs break up the face. It is mostly shaded by trees, though that shifts with the season, and it works as a decent warm-up spot for the neighboring roof wall.

tx_central_wall.blurb: Central Wall is a large face on the west flank of North Mountain at Hueco Tanks, in far West Texas near El Paso. It carries 19 routes, mostly trad with a smaller group of bolted sport lines, and several of them stretch to two or three pitches. Grades run from 5.7 up to a couple of 5.12s and one 5.13, but the bulk of the climbing sits at 5.10. It is a rare spot at this park for roped, multi-pitch climbing in a place better known for bouldering, so bring a rack and a rope rather than pads.

tx_lunch_rocks.blurb: Lunch Rocks is a scattering of boulders on North Mountain at Hueco Tanks, beside the road that runs past the front-side parking area, and a trail leads up to the blocks. Nearly all of its 19 climbs are boulder problems, with one top rope. The grades split into two camps: plenty of friendly problems from V0 to V3, then a tight cluster of V6 and V7 lines, with a V8 and a V10 at the top end. That mix suits groups with climbers of very different strength. Expect only a short walk from the road.

tx_dugout_east_the.blurb: The Dugout (East) is the main boulder field in the North Boulders section of Reimers Ranch, west of Austin. It sits a bit deeper in the canyon than the neighboring Dugout (West) and is reached by a short trail from the North Boulders lot. All 19 climbs are boulder problems, and most fall between V0 and V3, which makes it friendly for newer boulderers, with a few harder lines up to V6. The canyon is a jumble of big boulders, problems are close together, and landings are generally clear. After rain the canyon holds humidity, so dry, cool days climb best.

tx_dark_heart_the.blurb: The Dark Heart is a large, shady, room-like boulder cave on East Mountain at Hueco Tanks, in far West Texas. Its shelter from sun, wind and rain makes it a good fallback on poor-weather days. All 19 climbs are boulder problems with a wide spread: a few easy ones around V0 to V2, a middle band from V3 to V6, and a strong top end of V8 and V9 lines, including some of the area's best-known test pieces. The two headline problems are found near the entrance and at the back of the room.

tx_asylum_the.blurb: The Asylum is a tall formation on North Mountain at Hueco Tanks in far West Texas, cut off from the main mass by a lagoon. The problems lie on its far side, away from the road, spread over four main boulders. Of 17 climbs, 16 are boulder problems and one is a top rope. The grades reach well beyond the average for the park: a pile of easy-to-moderate problems around V2 to V3, a few mid-grade classics in the V5 to V7 range, and a hard tail running to V12. Reach it on foot along a marked trail through a small valley from the front-side lot.
